Subject: Post-demo recap: model proposals + locale-specific eval plan (EU & APAC)

Thanks again for the demo slot today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) Goals we heard
- LinguaHealth: automated triage and short-form summarization for multilingual support tickets across FR/DE/ES (EU) and JA/KO/HI (APAC). Primary constraints: <200ms token latency in p90 for short responses, stable per-language quality (human pass-rate >= 90% on intent/summary checks).
- GlobalRetail (Carlos): product Q&A in localized storefronts (EN-GB, FR, ES); need consistent entity extraction and low hallucination on SKUs.

2) Model fit suggestions (initial, based on workload & token profile)
- EU languages (FR/DE/ES): Redwood-recommended: Llama2-13B-chat-ft (quantized q4) for a balance of safety and cost; fallback to xglm-8B for very low-latency routes.
- APAC languages (JA/KO/HI): Suggest a specialized Japanese/Korean fine-tuned variant (proof-of-concept): Mosaic-JA-7B and Mosaic-KO-7B (we can spin localized fine-tunes); for Hindi, use multilingual-13B-checkpoint with IPA token handling.
- For strict hallucination constraints, propose an ensemble reranker (embed-based rerank + critic prompt) backed by Redwood’s reranking pipeline.

3) Eval artifacts I’ll share (attached and in Drive)
- benchmark_results_v1.csv — synthetic token-latency + automated metrics across sample set (per-locale BLEU/ROUGE/Exact Match, and Rouge-L proxies).
- prompt_candidates_2027-03-14.zip — 30 per-locale prompt templates we’d like you to sanity-check.
- MAP_draft_LinguaHealth.docx — draft mutual action plan with milestones: pilot data ingest, 48h pilot, 2-week expanded eval.

4) Quality/regression concerns to watch for
- Tokenization mismatches (esp. Hindi/Indic scripts) leading to off-by-one token drift in prompt prefix caching — can show up as subtle prompt degradation over long contexts.
- Ensemble/reranker sensitivity: reranker can amplify biases if its training prompts are skewed by EU-style formal register vs APAC informal samples.
- Metric gap: automatic metrics overstate JA/KO quality; plan human-in-the-loop spot checks for initial 1k responses per locale.

5) Proposed next steps (actionable)
- Neha (me) to grant Drive access + upload an additional 500 sample tickets by Tue 16 Mar. (Done: Drive link above.)
- Marissa to scope fine-tune cost and ETA for Mosaic-JA/KO variants (target estimate by Wed 17 Mar).
- Rishi + Alex to run a 48-hour pilot: enable two model routes (13B quantized vs 7B localized) and collect p90 latency + per-locale quality buckets. Start: Mon 22 Mar.
- Customer ask: Linh/Carlos to confirm 3 priority locales (reply with order-of-importance).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for “Pilot kickoff” once we have the confirmed pilot start date.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Thanks Neha — I reviewed the sample artifacts. Quick internal notes and a rough ETA: 

- Fine-tune cost & ETA: Mosaic-JA/KO fine-tune (7B) ~ $2.8K per locale for initial POC (12-18 hours GPU). Mosaic-HI de-prioritized for now; we’d first try multilingual-13B with tokenizer tweaks.
- Reranker cost: adding a lightweight embedding-based reranker increases per-query cost by ~12-18% depending on batch sizes; full critic (LM-based) adds ~40-60% but improves hallucination reduction by ~2-6% in our past benchmarks. I’ve attached a short cost model snapshot to Drive (REDC-2389).
- Eval plan: propose 1k automated samples + 200 human checks per locale. For JA/KO, need native annotators (we can spin contractors).

I’ll prepare a one-pager with the cost/ETA and a checklist for the pilot. Neha — I can be on the kickoff call. Rishi/Alex, please confirm availability for Mon 22 Mar if Linh confirms data upload.
